:::{#def-congruence}
#### Congruence modulo $n$

Let $a$ and $b$ be [integers](#def-integers),
and let $n$ be a [positive integer](#def-positive-integer).
We say that $a$ is **congruent to $b$ modulo $n$**,
written $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$,
if $n$ [divides](#def-divides) $a - b$, written $n \mid (a - b)$,
[@wikipedia_modular_arithmetic].
When $a$ is not congruent to $b$ modulo $n$,
we write $a \not\equiv b \pmod{n}$.

:::
